props.description:
Per-family prop overrides, keyed by family id — the studio's knobs.
A family with no entry renders on its own defaults.

props.description:
Per-family custom-property declarations, keyed by family id, applied to
that layer alone.
Scoped per layer rather than set on a shared ancestor because the one
token every family DOES share — `--backdrop-ground` — has to differ per
layer: the bottom one paints the plate and the rest are forced
transparent. Everything else is prefixed per family in `tokens.css`.

props.description: An authored composition, applied to the first Möbius layer only.

props.name: labels
props.description: Studio affordances, forwarded to the composed Möbius layer.

props.name: group
props.description: Render only one popover's worth. Omit for the whole list.

props.name: showReset
props.description: The reset button belongs to the studio's toolbar, not every popover.

props.name: defaults
props.description:
What "unmodified" means for THIS list, and what Reset restores.
A parameter because the panel now draws two different knob sets: the
Möbius backdrop's, and whichever standalone family is selected.
Comparing a family's knobs against the Möbius defaults would find no
match for any of them and report the whole panel as untouched.

props.name: hideAlpha
props.description:
Drop the alpha slider beside each swatch.
Alpha is first-class for a backdrop — it is the difference between a
backdrop and a foreground — and meaningless for a consumer that paints
opaque solids, like the character renderer, where a translucent facet
would just be a hole. Shipping the slider there anyway would be a
control that does nothing, which this file's own rule calls worse than
no control.

props.name: optionPreview
props.description:
Draw a choice knob's options as rendered previews instead of their names.
A name is enough to pick between `hollow | weight | plated`. It is not
enough to pick between thirty shield silhouettes — nobody can tell
`crestnotch` from `crestkey` from the word. The panel stays ignorant of
what it is drawing: the caller hands back a thumbnail for a given
(prop, option) pair, and the panel just lays them out.

props.name: preset
props.description: Which composition to open on.

props.name: onapply
props.description: Fired on Apply with everything authored here, for the caller to persist.

props.name: density
props.description: Particle count. 220 is the tuned default; past ~400 it muddies.

props.name: speed
props.description: Pixels a particle walks per step.

props.name: decay
props.description:
How much old ink is erased each step. 0.035 is the tuned value: lower
and trails smear forever, higher and they read as dashes.

props.name: maxDpr
props.description: Device pixel ratio ceiling.

props.name: count
props.description: How many bands. Three reads as strata; six reads as noise.

props.name: speed
props.description:
Multiplies every band's period. The far/near SPREAD is preserved — the
layers moving at different speeds is what carries the depth — so this
scales the whole set rather than flattening it toward one rate.

props.name: strips
props.description:
The strips to draw, explicitly. Each is addressable and independently
placed — pass this when tuning. Omit and the backdrop seeds its own,
which is what shipping code does.

props.name: labels
props.description: Show each strip's id on the stage, so "strip 2" has a referent.

props.name: selected
props.description: Which id is highlighted while being edited.

props.name: count
props.description: How many strips to seed when `strips` is omitted.

props.name: seed
props.description: Deterministic scatter — same seed, same arrangement every load.

props.name: hero
props.description: Seed one large centred strip instead of a scatter.

props.name: rainbow
props.description:
Sweep a continuous hue along the chain instead of using the flat strip
colour. Each strip is one step further round the wheel, so the rainbow
reads as one band of colour travelling a1 → a2 → a3 → b1 → …, not as
six independently cycling objects.

props.name: preset
props.description:
Load a named composition — the builder's and the app shell's way in,
since neither can express a `StripSpec[]` as a prop.
An explicit `strips` array always wins: the studio passes live,
half-edited state and must not have it replaced by the preset it
started from.
A preset that carries a palette applies it to THIS component's wrapper
rather than to `:root`. Two backdrops on one page then stay
independent, and dropping one into an editor does not repaint the
editor around it.

props.name: onselect
props.description: Fired when a strip's tag is clicked. Only reachable when `labels`.

props.name: levels
props.description: Iso-levels. More is busier, not deeper.

props.name: seed
props.description: Field seed — a different landscape, same character.

props.name: angle
props.description: Hatch angle in degrees.

props.name: ground
props.description:
The ground the near band paints with. MUST match the page behind it,
 or the occluding fill reads as a grey smear instead of a hole.

props.name: stripColor
props.description: `r, g, b`. Defaults are the spider-verse palette's own values.

props.name: stripColor2
props.description:
Second stop. The band is painted with a gradient across its own extent
rather than a flat colour, so the hue travels along the ribbon and the
far and near laps are never quite the same — which reads as one long
object turning through space instead of two arcs of the same paint.
Set equal to `stripColor` for a flat strip.

props.name: gap
props.description: Lattice spacing. Below ~14px the two sets fuse into flat tone.

props.name: angle
props.description: Angle of the first line set. The second is offset off-square.

props.name: strips
props.type: { spec: StripSpec; index: number; layout: MobiusLayout }[]
props.description: One entry per spec, carrying the layout that spec built.

props.name: flowing
props.description: Rainbow mode — the hue sweeps along the chain instead of per strip.

props.name: energyPeriod
props.description:
The chain-wide energy clock, seconds. One value for every strip, or the
 pulse stops crossing between them and becomes six blinkers.

props.name: camera
props.description:
The Canvas camera, when the backdrop is inside one. Read per frame and
 never written — a GL layer that owns a camera drifts off the SVG drawn
 beside it.

props.name: rainbowBase
props.description:
Saturated stand-in for rainbow mode; `hue-rotate` cannot invent
 saturation out of the ground's near-grey.

props.name: opacity
props.description:
How present the floor is. It is scenery — at 1 the rails compete with
 whatever is standing on them.

props.name: rails
props.description: Rails, and cross-lines. More of either reads as graph paper.

props.name: size
props.description:
The shield's width in px, read the same way `ArmornetCrestChrome` reads
 it — not the line crest's own box.

props.name: loose
props.description:
Draw the figure separately from the wall. Off, this is the shipped
 logo; on, the mark is in two pieces and `spin` moves one of them.

props.name: spin
props.description: The figure's azimuth, radians. Whole turns land back on the rest pose.

props.name: ignite
props.description:
How far the hub has caught, 0–1. Runs the wall from graphite to the
 accent and the figure one stage further, toward white.

props.name: pulse
props.description:
The hot core's own flicker, 0–1. Separate from `ignite` because a
 steady bloom reads as a gradient rather than as something burning.

props.name: breathe
props.description:
A scale on the whole mark. The breath, when a host has a clock to
 drive it with.

props.name: size
props.description:
The forged mark's rendered width, px. Everything in the scene is
 resolved against it.

props.name: floor
props.description:
The room the mark stands in. Off leaves it on the background ramp
 alone, which is what a host with its own backdrop wants.

props.name: t
props.description:
The clock, ms. Bindable so a scrubber can drive it; left alone the
 component runs it.

props.name: oncomplete
props.description:
Fired once, when the mark has finished arriving AND the lamp has had
 long enough to say so. A host that swaps this out for its own screen
 waits on this rather than on a duration it has copied.

props.name: t
props.description:
Bind these to drive the studio from outside — a page with its own
 toolbar, or a test that wants to park on one frame.

props.name: keys
props.description:
Take the keyboard. On for a full-screen route; off when the studio is
 one block on a page of them, where a stray `space` would be a surprise.

props.name: size
props.description:
Rendered width, px. The contours are authored in the forged cut's
 200×220 box and scale with it.

props.name: edges
props.description: The contours to light — `buildEdges()`, or any subset of it.

props.name: lamp
props.description:
Where the light is. `z` is how far in front of the face it hangs: near
 enough to pick out edges one at a time, far enough not to blow out
 whatever it passes over.

props.name: figure
props.type: { hub: Pt; nodes: Pt[]; hubR: number; nodeR: number }
props.description:
The mesh figure's joints, so the solid parts of the mark are lit too.
 Omit and only the contours answer — which the eye reads immediately as
 a shield that is lit with a mark sitting on it that is not.

props.name: shield
props.description:
The silhouette the face passes are clipped to. Without it the brushed
 field and the streak are a rectangle over the artwork.

props.name: intensity
props.description:
Fade the whole lamp up. Every pass reads it, so this is the light
 arriving rather than an opacity over a lit picture.

props.name: offsetY
props.description:
Px to lift the artboard by, so the SHIELD's centre — not the 200×220
 box's — lands on the host's centre. `0.005784 × size` is what the
 forged cut needs; a scene registers every layer against the same
 point or the light drifts off the thing it is lighting.

props.name: size
props.description: Rendered width, px. Coordinates are the forged cut's 200×220 box.

props.name: cx
props.description: The point the rings leave from, in box units.

props.name: t
props.description:
Ms since the event. Before 0 and after the last ring lands, nothing
 renders.

props.name: direction
props.description:
Which way. `out` is a shock; `in` is the one thing in a collapse that
 travels toward the middle, which is why it reads at all.

props.name: stagger
props.description:
Ms between rings — one number for an even pulse, or one per ring when
 the spacing itself should be uneven (which is what turns a pulse into a
 detonation).

props.name: duration
props.description: How long one ring takes to travel `reach`.

props.name: from
props.description: Start radius and travel, box units.

props.name: ease
props.description: `quint` is a hit — full speed on the first frame. `cubic` is a shove.

props.name: peak
props.description:
Peak opacity, and how sharply it falls off. A high `tail` puts the whole
 ring's life in its first third, which is what a blast looks like.

props.name: width
props.description: Stroke width as `[base, gain]` — `base + gain × opacity`.

props.name: leadColor
props.description:
The first ring's colour, when the leading edge of a detonation should be
 hotter than what follows it.

props.name: blend
props.description: Screen-blend, for a shock that has to stay bright over what it crosses.

props.name: offsetY
props.description:
Px to lift the artboard by, so the rings are centred on the same point
 every other layer in the scene is registered against.

props.name: size
props.description:
Layer size in px; the layer is square and maps the chrome box the way
 `ArmornetCrestChrome` does, so box coords line up with the scene.

props.name: t
props.description: ms into the assembly beat. Negative renders nothing.

props.name: targets
props.description: Seats, in chrome-box coords, and when each should be arrived at.

props.name: accent
props.description: Overrides the `--accent` token.

props.name: repeat
props.description:
Sparks per target. Left off, the field fills toward a frame density
 rather than inheriting however finely the caller tiled the mark.

props.name: reach
props.description: Run-up length in box units — see `BuildOpts.reach`.

props.name: decay
props.description:
How much of the old trail is erased each frame. 0.22 is the tuned value:
lower and the comets stretch until they read as static beams, higher and
they shorten into dashes with a visible head.

props.name: offsetY
props.description:
Px to lift the field by, so it is centred on the same point as the mark
 it is building rather than on the artboard.

props.name: x
props.description: Viewport coordinates of the click that opened it.

props.name: onrename
props.description: Hand renaming back to the layers panel, which owns the inline input.

props.name: scale
props.description: Canvas zoom, so the chrome can stay a constant size on screen.

props.name: onAdd
props.description: Double-click on a card — hosts that can place centre wire this up.

props.name: showSearch

Show the Templates tab. Off by default: a template is a whole canvas
arrangement, which only makes sense where there is a canvas to drop it
on — the scene palette has no use for it.

props.description: CSS declarations applied to the wrapper, e.g. theme studio overrides.

props.name: scale
props.description: Canvas zoom, so the chrome can stay a constant size on screen.

props.name: valueOf
props.description: Resolve a token to its current value (override or theme default).

props.name: pov
props.description:
A second way of looking at the character, rendered instead of the
turntable when the stage is switched to it.
A SNIPPET rather than an import, and that is the whole design. The thing
this slot exists for is breach's first-person cutaway, which knows about
cards, shots and a board — none of which `src/lib` may know about, since
a library that imports an example has been turned inside out. So the
studio declares a hole the shape of "given this character, draw
something", and the route that mounts both fills it.
Absent, the toggle does not appear at all: a mode switch with one mode is
a control that does nothing.

props.description: What to call it on the toggle.

props.name: crop
props.description: `hero` fits the whole figure; `bust` and `chip` crop to the head.

props.name: shadow

props.name: art

Camera and suit. Omitted everywhere but the studio — a roster wants
 one angle for all four, or the tiles stop being comparable.

Custom hover popover. When provided, this renders at the cursor in place of the
default ChartTooltip. Lets any chart (donut, lollipop, heatmap) supply rich markup.

The scale's segments. The filled arc is CUT at these boundaries rather than
painted one colour to the reading: a single hue covers the very bands it is
meant to be read against, leaving a dial that has colour on it but says
nothing with it.

fields.description: Degrees of arc the scale spans. Default 240.

fields.description:
Where the scale starts, in SVG degrees (0 = 3 o'clock, growing clockwise).
Default 150, which opens the gauge downward and centres it on 12 o'clock.

Gauge only. The READING comes from the first point of the first visible
series, the SCALE from `yAxis.domain` (default [0, 100]), and every marked
value — a pass gate, a peer median, an SLA — from `annotations` with
`axis: 'y'`. Only what is genuinely gauge-specific lives here, so a caller
already fluent in the other chart types has one new object to learn.

props.name: shape
props.description:
Which silhouette to forge. 'traced' is this component's own hand-traced
shield carrying the A monogram; anything else is a shield from
`ArmornetCrestMesh` carrying the crestlink figure.
Shape and figure move TOGETHER on purpose. The A's joints and feet were
traced against the traced shield's exact proportions — its bar sits
where that silhouette is widest — so dropping it into a notched or
clipped crown puts the apex under a slot and the feet in the taper.

props.name: glow
props.description: Bloom under the shield and behind the joints.

props.name: bloom
props.description: Bloom strength, 0–1. Ignored when `glow` is off.

props.name: traces
props.description: Faint circuitry etched into the glass. Drop it below ~64px.

props.name: rim
props.description: The second border floating inside the frame.

props.name: emboss
props.description: Cast shadow seating the mark into the glass.

props.name: tethers
props.description:
Struts tying every joint out to the shield wall — the A stops floating
 in the field and becomes structure the shield carries.

props.name: breakout
props.description:
0–1. How far the A grows PAST the shield boundary: at 1 the apex crosses
 the crown and the feet cross the lower flanks, so the mark reads as
 overlaid on the shield rather than contained by it.

props.name: look
props.description:
How the letter separates itself from the mesh:
  'hollow' — members stroked wide with their core cut out (default)
  'weight' — one solid weight, heavier than the mesh
  'plated' — solid members over a soft wide underplate
'plated' leans on opacity; prefer 'hollow' or 'weight' for one-colour
reproduction.

props.name: spokes
props.description:
Which spokes leave the hub, on top of the bar it always sits on:
  'full' — stem up to the apex and down to both feet (default)
  'stem' — stem only
  'bar'  — none, so the A's counter stays open

props.name: tethers
props.description: The tethers binding the A to the shield wall. Drop them below ~32px.

props.name: glow
props.description: Blurred underlay behind the mark — atmosphere, not structure.

props.name: color
props.description: Brand colour of the whole mark.

props.name: meshColor
props.description: Overrides the interior only. Defaults to `color` — the mark is monochrome.

props.name: shape

props.name: innerWall

props.name: glow
props.description: Blurred underlay behind the mark — atmosphere, not structure.

props.name: color
props.description: The whole mark. Monochrome by design — one colour, one weight.

props.name: variant
props.description:
'filled' inverts it: a solid shield with the figure punched through to
whatever is behind, so a dark-on-light lockup needs no second asset.

props.name: innerWall
props.description: The hairline inside the shield wall. Drop it below ~32px — it silts up.

props.name: glow
props.description: Blurred underlay. Atmosphere; off for anything that has to reproduce flat.

props.name: mark
props.description:
Which mark the studio opens on — every block on the icons page has its
 own way in, and landing on the wrong one is a hunt.

props.name: icon
props.description:
Which glyph, when the way in was a cell of the icon grid: you clicked
 `fingerprint`, so `fingerprint` is what is on the stage.

props.name: shape
props.description:
Same idea for the shield grids: you clicked `merlon`, so the shield
 knob opens on `merlon` rather than on the mark's default.

props.name: sidebar
props.description:
Full sidebar content — rendered in the desktop aside and the mobile drawer.
 Receives whether the desktop rail is collapsed to icons, so the sidebar can
 swap its expandable tree for a flat icon rail. Always false in the mobile drawer.

props.name: mobileBrand
props.description: Brand/logo area shown in the mobile top bar (alongside the hamburger).

props.name: toolbar
props.description: Optional toolbar rendered at the top of the main content area (sticky).

props.name: sidebarWidth
props.description: Width of the desktop sidebar column. Default: 220px.

props.name: iconRail
props.description:
Make the desktop sidebar collapsible via an edge-carat toggle:
- Expanded (default): the full `sidebarWidth` sidebar with each item's
  label to the RIGHT of its icon.
- Collapsed: a bare `railWidth` icon rail. Icons hold the exact position
  they had when expanded (no shuffle), and each label reappears as a
  hover tooltip just past the rail's right edge.
The choice persists across reloads.

props.name: railWidth
props.description: Width of the collapsed (icon-only) rail. Default: 64px.

props.name: rawContent
props.description:
Skip the automatic PagePanel wrapper. Use for pages that own their
own full-bleed layout (e.g. console, canvas pages).

props.name: lockScroll
props.description:
Optionally disable page-level scrolling on the main content area.
- `'x'`  — clip horizontal overflow so nothing scrolls past the right
           edge (e.g. a fixed toolbar rail); vertical page scroll stays.
- `'y'`  — pin to the viewport height; the page won't scroll down.
- `'both'` — full lock; inner regions must own their own scrolling.
Defaults to no lock.

props.name: ground
props.description:
How strongly to paint the glass ground behind the page.
- `'deep'` (default) — half-strength aurora and a soft, ramped grid.
  The right choice under dense content, where a full-strength wash
  competes with tables and forms.
- `'bright'` — the full aurora and the crisp hairline grid. For pages
  where the ground is part of the composition rather than a backdrop:
  canvases, and low-density showpieces like first-run onboarding.

props.name: horizon
props.description:
Add the horizon layer to the ground: two planes raked to a vanishing
point at the centre line, with their cross-ties travelling toward the
viewer. A flat grid reads as a surface; a converging one reads as
distance, which is what makes the content feel like it sits in front
of something rather than on it.
Off by default. It is a backdrop, so it is deliberately something a
page opts into rather than something every page inherits — and its
strength is `--glass-horizon`, not a hardcoded alpha, so it can be
dialled per theme or switched off entirely without touching markup.

props.name: backdrop
props.description:
A named backdrop composition, or `none`. Supersedes `horizon`, which
stays for callers that just want the default ground and have no opinion
about which one.

props.name: backdropStrength
props.description: 0–1, applied to the backdrop layer as `--backdrop-strength`.

props.name: mark
props.description:
Small-caps wordmark above the statement. The leading glyph is drawn in
 the accent; pass the mark without it.

props.name: statement
props.description:
The statement, as its two halves. The face switches between them mid
 sentence — the machine finishes the human's sentence — which is the
 whole idea, and why this is two strings rather than one.

props.name: sub
props.description: One supporting sentence. Anything longer wants a different screen.

props.name: step
props.description:
Where you are in the flow, e.g. `01 / WORKSPACE`. Numbering is earned:
 it says what a bare "Sign in." heading could not.

props.name: form
props.description:
The flow itself — fields, provider buttons, whatever the step needs.
 Style its contents with the `auth-*` classes this component publishes
 (see the style block) rather than with CSS in the route.

props.name: aside
props.description: Footer under the form. Typically the "new here?" line.

props.name: visual
props.description:
The left pane, in place of the statement — for a screen whose left half
 IS the thing rather than a claim about it (a live board, a preview).
 It fills the pane edge to edge, so `mark`/`statement`/`sub` are ignored
 when it is given. The flow's own heading then has to live on the right,
 which is what `.auth-title` is for.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra CSS classes on the root element.

props.name: raisedEdgeIds
props.description:
Edges painted ABOVE the nodes instead of beneath them. Edges are otherwise
 drawn first, so a link between two distant nodes disappears under every
 node it passes; raising one keeps a link the operator just made visible
 across the whole canvas.

props.name: showGrid
props.description: Background grid. Off for ambient / marketing canvases.

props.name: allowNodeDrag
props.description: Node dragging. Off for passive canvases that only select + hover.

props.name: allowLinkDraw
props.description: Port-to-port link drawing. Off for read-only meshes.

props.name: edgeCurve
props.description:
'line' = straight port-to-port · 'bezier' = horizontal-eased curve ·
 'bow' = quadratic bowed perpendicular to the link, so two nodes joined by
 several links fan apart instead of overprinting.

props.name: insetLeafLabels
props.description:
For ringed leaf-icon nodes that carry a value, draw a smaller glyph and
 stack the label + value INSIDE the disc instead of below it. Used by the
 overview globe so every mode reads as a self-contained token.

props.name: unselectedDim
props.description:
How far a node unrelated to the selection is faded, 0..1.
 1 leaves the mesh untouched. Low values make selection read as isolation:
 right when the neighbours are context you are finished with, wrong when
 they are the answer to "where am I" — which is what they are on a globe
 the camera has just flown you across.

props.name: glBodies
props.description:
A GL layer is drawing the solids, so don't draw them here.
 Only the BODY is withheld. The hit proxy, caption and beacon stay, because
 they are the parts that must be pointed at, read by a screen reader, or
 laid out against other text — none of which a GPU does for free.

props.name: labelScale
props.description:
Scale the node NAME relative to everything else in the disc.
 The default sizing assumes a mesh label is a short code (`DEP·ANALYSIS`)
 sitting above a readout that is the point of the node. A layer whose
 labels ARE the content — a roadmap initiative — needs the opposite
 emphasis, and scaling it here keeps the wrap, the chord and the readout
 offsets all consistent with the new size.

props.name: typeLabels
props.description:
Print the node's TYPE above its name (`AGENTIC`, `PROXY`, …).
 That taxonomy is the mesh's own, so a layer borrowing these silhouettes
 to stand for something else — a roadmap initiative, say — would be
 labelling every node with a word that means nothing in its domain.

props.name: depthSortedParticles
props.description:
Give edge particles the same paint depth as their line. By default the
 particle stream is drawn ABOVE every node so energy is never occluded; on
 the globe that floats back-of-sphere energy over the near nodes. When set,
 base-edge particles paint behind the nodes (raised-edge particles still
 ride on top), so energy weaves through depth like the static web does.

props.name: onFacetSelect
props.type: (nodeId: string, mode: string, index: number) => void
props.description:
A fanned-out mode facet was clicked. `index` is the facet's occurrence
 among same-mode facets (0-based), for instance-precise targeting.

props.name: onNodeHover
props.type: (id: string | null, screenPos: { x: number; y: number } | null) => void
props.description:
Hover enter/leave with the cursor position in layer-local screen space,
 so a parent can float a card next to it. Null on leave.

props.name: nodes
props.description:
Logical nodes INCLUDING the hub. Positions are ignored on entry — this
 component owns them.

props.name: edges
props.description:
Edges are pure passthrough — bind them so a draft link the operator draws
 writes straight back to the caller's array (MeshStudio adds it there).

props.name: layout
props.description:
The arrangement. Bindable so the on-canvas arrangement control (see
 `layoutPicker`) can change it without a header sitting above the canvas.

props.name: hubId
props.description: Which node is the crest — the fixed centre of every layout.

props.name: camera
props.description: The <Canvas> camera handle, exposed so the caller can fly to a node.

props.name: onFacetSelect
props.type: (nodeId: string, mode: string, index: number) => void

props.name: concept
props.description: MeshStudio passthroughs.

props.name: nodeR
props.description: Default footprint radius for a node that declares none.

props.name: margin
props.description: Placement clearances (px).

props.name: laneClearance
props.description: Radial only — hold each hub→spoke line clear, up to this many spokes.

props.name: groupKeyOf
props.description: Grouping key per node for the 'grouped' layout (defaults to one group).

props.name: radiusOf
props.description:
A node's FOOTPRINT radius for placement — the room it actually occupies once
connection rings, captions and fanned facets are counted, which can exceed
the drawn disc radius (`r`). Defaults to `r`; a caller that draws rings around
nodes should pass the larger footprint so they don't overlap.

props.name: globeSensitivity
props.description: Globe tuning.

props.name: globeFrontFade
props.description:
How much a node dims between the point nearest the eye and the limb, on
 the side you can see. Small on purpose — this is atmosphere, and the
 moment it is strong enough to notice as an effect it is reading as a
 vignette instead of as distance.

props.name: globeControls
props.description:
Show the on-canvas globe controls (spin / reset / auto-rotate / zoom),
 bottom-right. Only rendered in the 'globe' layout.

props.name: layoutPicker
props.description:
Show the arrangement picker in the same on-canvas control cluster. Unlike
 the globe rows it renders in EVERY layout — otherwise leaving 'globe'
 would take the only way back with it.

props.name: autoRotateSpeed
props.description: Radians the globe advances per auto-rotate frame.

props.name: autoRotate
props.description:
Whether the globe is auto-rotating. Bindable so the on-canvas toggle and a
 caller can share the state; pass `true` to start spinning by default.

props.name: axialTilt
props.description:
Radians the spin axis tips toward the viewer, giving a planet-like tilted
 spin instead of a flat upright turn. 0 keeps the axis vertical.

props.name: insetLeafLabels
props.description:
Draw ringed leaf nodes with a smaller glyph and the label + value stacked
 inside the disc (passed through to MeshStudio).

props.name: typeLabels
props.description:
Print the node's TYPE as an eyebrow above its name (passed through to
 MeshStudio). On a mesh of infrastructure the kind of node is half the
 story; on a mesh whose labels are already real names it is the same word
 stamped on everything. Defaults on, matching MeshStudio.

props.name: tuning
props.description:
Per-canvas overrides on the studio's draw knobs, merged over DEFAULT_TUNING.
 For a caller that has to change what the canvas DRAWS from its own controls
 — a mesh big enough that per-link rings or per-link labels stop being
 legible needs to turn them off from the page, not from the demo cog.

props.name: globeIntro
props.description:
Play the orbit fly-in once when the globe layout first appears. Off by
 default; the DevCog can always replay it regardless.

props.name: globeLabel
props.description: Label for this globe in the DevCog's globe controls.

props.name: globeFill
props.description:
How much bigger than a tight fit the globe reads. 1 fits it exactly; 1.2
 makes the sphere fill 20% more of the frame. Node discs are counter-scaled
 by the same factor, so they keep the size they had at the tight fit and the
 extra room goes into the space BETWEEN them.

props.name: hudInsets
props.description:
Edges of the canvas that floating chrome (stat cards, tickers, controls)
 occupies. The globe is fitted to — and centred in — what is left, so a node
 is never placed underneath a panel. Pixels.

props.name: focusOnSelect
props.description:
Selecting a node turns the globe until that node faces the viewer.
 Off by default. An unrequested camera move is disorienting on a mesh
 where selection only means "show me the details" — it is the pairing with
 a drawer that turns it into navigation rather than the globe wandering.

props.name: focusDurationMs
props.description:
How long that turn takes, ms. Long enough to read as the globe rotating
 and not as a cut; short enough that it never feels like waiting.

props.name: focusTilt
props.description:
Radians the focused node is lifted ABOVE the middle of the disc, so a
 solid standing there is seen head-on instead of from directly overhead.
 0 centres it exactly — which is the worst view of a building there is.

props.name: focusDistance
props.description:
View distance, in globe radii, the camera closes to on focus. Lower is
 nearer. Below about 1.8 the perspective divide gets violent and the near
 limb starts to bow.

props.name: focusContext
props.description:
How much room the jib leaves around the focused node, in multiples of its
 own radius. 1 crops to the node itself; larger keeps more of the ground it
 is standing on. Too tight and the subject loses the terrain that says
 where it is — the point is a building IN a landscape, not a portrait.

props.name: focusZoomSteps
territoryDistance
props.description:
View distance, in globe radii, a flight to a TERRITORY closes to. Further
 out than `focusDistance` on purpose: the subject is a region several nodes
 across, and diving to node range crops the very grouping being shown.

props.name: territoryContext
props.description:
How much room a territory flight leaves around the region, as a multiple of
 the cap's own projected radius. Above 1 keeps the borders either side of it
 in shot, which is what makes it read as one region among several.

props.name: glPieces
props.description:
Draw the buildings with WebGL2 instead of SVG.
 Opt-in while both renderers exist. The SVG path stays the fallback for a
 browser without WebGL2 — `GlobePieces` reports that itself and draws
 nothing, so the switch is also the A/B: same scene, same camera, one
 renderer swapped, measurable with the QA cog's frame capture.

props.name: globeTerritories
props.description:
Pack the globe into TERRITORIES — one region per `groupKeyOf` key — rather
 than sowing every node evenly over the sphere. Needs `groupKeyOf`; without
 one there are no groups to divide the surface into and it is ignored.
 A grouped globe is necessarily BIGGER than an even one at the same node
 size: the empty borders between regions are surface that no node may use,
 and that space is the entire reason a region reads as a region.

props.name: territoryOf
props.description:
How to NAME and tint a territory. Returning null leaves the region unnamed
 (still clustered — just not captioned). Only consulted when
 `globeTerritories` is on.

props.name: territoryFraction
props.description:
Share of the sphere the regions may occupy between them; the rest is the
 border. Passed straight to `packSphereClusters`.

props.name: focusTerritory
props.description:
Which territory the globe currently holds in focus — the one it tints.
 Reported OUT (bindable) so a caller listing the territories can light the
 same row the globe is lighting, whether the focus came from
 `flyToTerritory` or from clicking a node that happens to live there.

props.name: territoryWallHeight
props.description:
How far a territory wall stands off the sphere, in GLOBE RADII — so it
 keeps its proportion however big the sphere packs. 0 lays it flat back on
 the surface. Bindable, and driveable live from the QA cog.

props.name: pieceLean
props.description:
How far a 3D node piece leans back toward the viewer, RADIANS.
 0 stands every piece straight up out of the sphere, which is honest and
 unreadable: a piece at the centre of the visible disc is then seen from
 directly overhead, and a house and a factory have the same roof. The lean
 is constant in camera space — see `tangentFrame` for why it must be
 constant rather than strongest where it is most needed.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
Ground under the globe. Without one the sphere is perfectly smooth, and
 anything standing on it can only ever sit ON the surface — there is
 nothing to sit IN. With one, every node rides its own elevation and a
 piece is buried to its footings in the patch beneath it.

props.name: relief
props.description:
Half-range of the terrain's elevation, in globe radii. Small: this is
 ground for the mesh to stand on, not a landscape to look at.

props.name: pieceSink
props.description:
How deep a piece sits in the ground, in node radii. Enough that the
 ground closes over its footings; more and the building sinks.

props.name: globeSurface
props.description:
Which globe you get, as ONE switch:
  · 'relief' — ground, solids standing in it, walls standing up.
  · 'flat'   — a smooth sphere, disc nodes, walls lying on the surface.
 One switch and not three, because the three are not independent: a
 building on a smooth sphere sits on nothing, and a wall standing up
 around flat markers is a fence around a diagram. Each set is coherent
 with itself, and the two are what a viewer would call two views.
 It changes only how the globe is DRAWN. The pack, the camera and the
 territories are identical in both, so switching never moves a node.

props.name: cx
props.description: Centre of the globe, in canvas coords.

props.name: radius
props.description: The sphere the nodes sit on — the same radius they were placed with.

props.name: viewDistance
props.description: Must match the projection the nodes use, or the web won't sit under them.

props.name: meridians
props.description: Lines of longitude — full great circles through both poles.

props.name: parallels
props.description:
Lines of latitude between the poles. Poles themselves are a point, not a
 circle, so they are never drawn.

props.name: surface
props.description:
How solid the globe's interior is, 0..1.
 What actually sells it as a body is that the canvas GRID stops at its
 edge — an object you can't see the floor through. So the interior is
 filled with the page background rather than tinted with the accent: a
 tint recolours the grid, it doesn't hide it.
 Not 1: the far side still has to show through, or spinning the globe
 stops being a way to find anything and the depth cues have nothing to
 act on.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
The ground, MASKED to the territories.
 The grid has to ride the same terrain the land does, or there are two
 surfaces: a wireframe sphere, and a wireframe landscape hovering over it
 with the sphere's own lines showing through from underneath. Nothing then
 looks joined, because nothing IS — the nodes stand on one and the globe
 is the other.
 A masked field makes this safe as well as right: it is exactly zero
 outside every region, so the grid stays on the sphere everywhere there is
 no land and rises only where there is. One surface, continuous, and the
 shore is where it meets itself.

props.name: relief
props.description: Height of the highest ground, in globe radii.

props.name: terrain
props.description:
The ground. A territory is not an outline on a sphere — it is a piece of
 LAND, and its floor is drawn as a contour web rising out of the surface.
 What is between territories gets no floor and no web: not sea, nothing.
 Expected to be cut to these same caps (see terrain `maskTerrain`), so the
 land falls to the surface exactly at the shore.

props.name: relief
props.description: Height of the highest ground, in globe radii.

props.name: contourInterval
props.description:
Elevation between neighbouring contour lines, in the field's own units
 (a masked terrain runs 0..1). The map's scale, and the one knob that
 decides how much ink the floor costs — halving it doubles the lines
 everywhere. Every 5th comes out as a heavier index contour.
 Set against the field's REAL range, not its nominal one. `maskTerrain`
 lifts to 0..1, but the interior of a region only reaches roughly 0.25–0.75
 — summed waves almost never peak together — so an interval chosen for the
 full range yields two or three lines and an empty-looking map.

props.name: moving
props.description:
Whether the camera is currently flying. Drops the per-frame-expensive
 ornament — see the bloom on the wall below — for as long as nobody could
 see it anyway.

props.name: value
props.description: The active layout. Bindable.

props.name: options
props.description: Options to offer. Defaults to the full MESH_LAYOUTS set.

props.name: label
props.description: Heading above the grid.

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns in the option grid.

props.name: count
props.description: Badge on the button — e.g. how many filters the caller has applied.

props.name: children
props.description: Extra popover content below the arrangement picker (filters, folding…).

props.name: vendors
props.description: Third-party vendors monitored via threat feeds + the vendor agent.

props.name: vendorAgentLabel
props.description: Label for the auto-added vendor-agent node. Default 'VENDOR AGENT'.

props.name: threatFeedLabel
props.description: Label for the auto-added threat-feeds source node. Default 'THREAT FEEDS'.

props.name: seen
props.description: Telemetry counters printed over the canvas.

props.name: animate
props.description: Boot cascade + count-up on mount. Default true.

props.name: ambient
props.description: Periodic block-flares once settled. Default true.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Enables hover preview + click detail card. Default false (pure ambient).

props.name: height
props.description: CSS height of the hero.

props.name: layout
props.description:
Node arrangement. 'membrane' (default) is the native left→right trust-
gradient pipeline (world → guards → core in fixed columns). The other five
are the SAME options the agent-management mesh offers — 'grouped', 'packed',
'radial', 'fan' and 'globe' — all arranged around the protected-core crest.
Bindable, so a picker can drive it.

props.name: showLayoutPicker
props.description: Show the arrangement picker docked over the canvas (drives `layout`).

props.name: ground
props.type: { x: number; y: number; near: boolean }[]

props.name: piece
props.description: `Structure.piece` — the catalogue key, not the structure id.

props.name: offline
props.description: Dims and dashes it, for a building nobody is holding.

props.name: index
props.description:
Which one is on the stage. Bindable so the page and the studio's own
 arrows move one selection rather than two that drift.

props.name: kind
props.description: Which effect to play. `none` renders nothing.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Replay key — increment to play again. 0 = idle (nothing shown).

props.name: anchorX
props.description: Origin of point bursts. Any CSS length/percent. Default: centre.

props.name: color
props.description: Accent colour for the particles. Defaults to the theme accent.

props.name: reverse
props.description:
Play the effect backwards — particles converge instead of scattering,
sweeps run the other way. Every effect is authored as an outward burst,
so this is a pure `animation-direction` flip rather than a second set of
keyframes: the closing half of a lifecycle is the opening half in
reverse, and stays that way for free as effects are added.

props.name: cluster
props.description:
Pinned block between the brand and the scrolling nav — e.g. a global
 Search / Inbox / My-work cluster. Stays put like brand/footer.

props.name: collapsed
props.description:
Icon-rail (collapsed) mode — centres the burst over the icon instead of
 anchoring it near the left edge of a full-width row.

props.name: active
props.description: The id of the currently active tab. Bindable.

props.name: sticky
props.description:
Pin the bar to the bottom of the scroll container and give it a card
border, so the commit action stays reachable on a long form instead of
living at the far end of the scroll.

props.name: hint
props.description:
Status text between the two ends — what committing does right now.
Pushes any `end` actions to the right edge.

props.name: trigger
props.description: Custom trigger snippet — receives `{ open }`. Defaults to the ⋮ kebab button.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the default kebab trigger.

props.name: closeOnSelect
props.description:
Whether picking an item closes the menu. Default true — one action, done.
Pass false for a multi-select set (`selected` on every item), where
closing after each tick makes choosing three things cost three openings.

props.name: footer
props.description:
Arbitrary content pinned below the items, under a separator — for the
one input a menu of choices cannot express (a free-text value, a link
out). Clicks inside it do not dismiss the menu. Keep it small: a menu
that grows a form is a popover wearing the wrong component.

props.name: autoDismiss
props.description:
Close the menu after a period of no hover and no focus, playing the
exit animation as the node is destroyed. Off unless asked for; see
`ACTIONS_MENU_DISMISS` for the shared defaults.
  autoDismiss                      → on, 2s, collapse
  autoDismiss={{ idleMs: 5000 }}   → on, 5s
  autoDismiss={false}              → off (the default)

props.name: ondismiss
props.description: Fired when the idle timer — not a click or Escape — closed the menu.

props.name: flourish
props.description:
Selection flourish played on the default kebab when it opens the menu.
Omit to follow the user's "Nav selection effect" theme setting, which is
the point — one preference drives the side nav and the kebabs alike.
Pass `'none'` to opt this menu out regardless of the setting.
Only applies to the built-in trigger: a custom `trigger` snippet is the
caller's markup, so its flourish is the caller's to render.

props.name: pressed
props.description:
Marks a `pill` as the active choice — fills it with `tone` and sets
aria-pressed, so a set of pills reads as a toggle group.

props.name: href
props.description: When set, renders as `<a>`; otherwise renders as `<button>`.

props.name: target
props.description: Anchor target — forwarded to `<a>` only.

props.name: full
props.description: Stretches the button to fill its container.

props.name: form
props.description: Associates the button with a form by id — forwarded to `<button form>`.

props.name: onquery
props.description:
Fires on every query change (and on open, with ''). Lets the host compute
live results (e.g. cross-entity search) and feed them back via `commands`.

props.name: externalFilter
props.description:
Host owns filtering: when true, `commands` is rendered verbatim (no internal
ranking pass) so the host can return its own ranked results — a host that
searches a live corpus knows things the label text does not. Pair with
`onquery`. Default false runs the built-in fuzzy ranking.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a subtle loading row (e.g. while a manifest/fetch is in flight).

props.name: formats
props.description: Formats to include. Defaults to all four.

props.name: icon
props.description: Override the trigger icon (default: download).

props.name: label
props.description: Tooltip / aria-label for the trigger button.

props.name: search
props.type: { value: string; set: (v: string) => void; placeholder?: string }

props.name: controls
props.description:
Page-specific control (e.g. a mesh layout picker) rendered at the start
 of the toolbar, before the standard filter/display controls.

props.name: tool
props.description:
What a plain left-drag means. `select` leaves the marquee in charge and
panning to the reserved gestures; `pan` hands the ordinary drag to the
camera, which is the only arrangement most people find without being
told. Defaults to `select` so every existing canvas is unchanged.

fields.name: angle
fields.description: Degrees. 0=right · 90=bottom · 180=left · 270=top.

props.name: onItemContextMenu
props.description:
Right-click on an item. The host owns the menu — the compositor only
 reports where it happened and makes sure the item is selected first.

props.name: connectMode
props.description: Click two items to wire them together instead of selecting them.

props.name: onConnectEnd
props.description:
Fired when a connector was drawn (or the gesture was abandoned), so the
 host can drop out of connect mode.

props.name: from
props.description: Where the line starts. Ignored when `d` is given.

props.name: to
props.description: Where it ends. Ignored when `d` is given.

props.name: d
props.description:
An explicit path, for anything the two routes below cannot express.
Takes precedence over `from`/`to`.

props.name: curve
props.description:
The shape of the run. `bow` is the mesh's default — see edge-path.ts
 for what each one is for and why the bow is clamped the way it is.

props.name: style
props.description: Transmission status. Sets the dash rhythm; see `EDGE_STYLE_DASH`.

props.name: dashOffset
props.description:
Where the dash pattern sits along the run, in px.
For a caller that drives its march off its own clock instead of taking
the CSS animation — a scene where every element has to be a pure
function of one time value, so a second free-running timer would drift
against everything else in it.
Only applies to a DASHED edge. A solid one reveals by animating this
same property, so honouring it there would fight the wipe.

props.name: dataType
props.description: What travels on it. Sets the colour, unless `color` overrides.

props.name: color
props.description:
Explicit colour. A legacy palette literal or a `--palette-*` name is
 resolved to the current theme's step — see theme/palette.svelte.ts.

props.name: flow
props.description:
Run a travelling orb along the line — the mesh's "this link is live"
 signal. Costs an `<animateMotion>`, so it is off by default.
 `'both'` adds a second orb running the other way, launched at the same
 moment, for a link that carries traffic in both directions rather than
 feeding one end. Same-instant and not staggered, matching the paired
 `scanning` particles in `MeshStudio`: two pulses crossing mid-run is
 the thing that reads as duplex, and phasing them apart turns it back
 into one orb shuttling. Opt-in, because direction is information — on
 a one-way link a returning orb is a claim we cannot make.

props.name: flowDur
props.description: Seconds for one traversal. Longer reads as further, not slower.

props.name: cap
props.description:
Draw a junction mark where the line ENDS. The mesh marks a termination,
 never a mid-run point — a dot in the middle reads as a node.

props.name: sharp
props.description:
Hard-edged rendering: butt line caps, and a SQUARE junction mark instead
of a dot.
The console is a rounded surface and the mesh's default matches it. The
marketing site is not — it is built on right angles, and a round cap
landing on a square node is the one detail that gives away that the
diagram came from somewhere else. Opt-in, so the app keeps its own vibe.

props.name: trimStart
props.description: Stop this many px short of `from` — the radius of whatever sits there.

props.name: trimEnd
props.description: Stop this many px short of `to`. See `trimSegment`.

props.name: revealed
props.description:
Whether the line is drawn in yet. `false` holds it hidden, `true` runs
the reveal, so a caller can gate the whole rail on one scroll trigger.
How it reveals depends on the style, because it has to: a solid line
WIPES (dashoffset over a normalised path length), but a line that
already carries a dash pattern cannot — the wipe and the pattern are the
same property, and animating one destroys the other. Those fade instead.

props.name: delay
props.description:
Seconds before this edge starts revealing. Staggering a bundle is what
 makes it read as wiring rather than an appearing picture.

props.name: tag
props.description: Eyebrow label — e.g. "ENG · 01". In rich mode, `docId` overrides this.

props.name: title
props.description: Main card title

props.name: meta
props.description: Footer metadata line — e.g. "DRAFT · 2026-05-13" (simple mode only)

props.name: variant
props.description: Accent color for the left edge bar, TR corner, and tag text

props.name: status
props.description: Status controls the dot color in the meta row. Rich mode accepts any string.

props.name: metaSlot
props.description: Optional override of the meta area (simple mode)

props.name: href
props.description: When set, the card renders as an anchor to this href.

props.name: icon
props.description: SVG path `d` for the header glyph — presence enables rich layout.

props.name: docId
props.description: Document identifier shown in the header (defaults to `tag`).

props.name: version
props.description: Version badge, rendered as `v{version}`.

props.name: classification
props.description: Classification label, shown at the top-right.

props.name: tags
props.description: Tag chips; overflow past `maxTags` collapses into a `+N` chip.

props.name: maxTags
props.description: Maximum tag chips before the `+N` overflow chip. Default 4.

props.name: authors
props.description: Author avatars (initials). First 3 are shown.

props.name: authorText
props.description: Fallback author byline when `authors` is empty.

props.name: updated
props.description: Date suffix appended to the status text (rich mode).

props.name: edge
props.description: Which edge the toolbar docks against.

props.name: toolbar
props.description: The docked rail. When omitted, the card renders content only.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the outer card (e.g. sizing / max-width).

props.name: contentClass
props.description: Classes for the content wrapper (padding, inner layout).

props.name: gradFrom
props.description: Tailwind gradient classes for the headline, e.g. 'from-[var(--accent)] to-[var(--palette-cyan)]'

props.name: shape
props.description: `'bracket'` (default) — L-bracket corners. `'cut-corner'` — diagonal clip + accent bars.

props.name: onclick
props.description: When set, renders as `<button>` so the whole card is interactive.

props.name: initials
props.description: Single letter or short initials displayed in the avatar box.

props.name: container
props.description: The frame — the thing being broken out of. Establishes the box.

props.name: overlay
props.description: The art that escapes. Centred on the container.

props.name: breakout
props.description: 0–1. How far the overlay breaks out. 0 leaves it contained.

props.name: grow
props.description: Overlay scale at breakout 1. 1.45 clears a shield-shaped container.

props.name: lift
props.description: Upward shift, % of container height, at breakout 1.

props.name: pad
props.description: Reserve flow space for the overhang.

props.name: originX
props.description:
Fractional origin the overlay grows about — 0.5/0.5 is its centre.
 Drop it below centre to push the growth upward.

props.name: open
props.description: Controls whether the content is visible. Bindable.

props.name: trigger
props.description:
Renders the trigger element. Receives `{ open, toggle }` so the
 caller can wire up any button or custom element as the trigger.

props.name: speed
props.description: Animation speed in seconds per revolution. Default 5s.

props.name: eyebrow
props.description: Short label shown beside the chevron toggle (e.g. "// vendor management").

props.name: crumbs
props.description:
Ancestors of this page, nearest-last, for a page reached by traversal
(register → risk, vendors → vendor → assessment). Every entry is a link:
the current page is the `eyebrow` beside the chevron, never a crumb, so a
trail never repeats where you already are. Omit on destination pages —
a trail of one is a decoration.

props.name: badge
props.description: Optional badge rendered inline after the eyebrow text (e.g. EarlyAccessBadge).

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph for an accent-bordered tile left of the title — identifies the subject.

props.name: sub
props.description: Mono line under the title, for the machine name of what the page configures.

props.name: meta
props.description:
Live status inline beside the title (e.g. "10 agents · 14 extensions").
Hidden under 900px, where the title needs the width more than the count does.

props.name: eyebrowActions
props.description: Controls/actions pinned to the right of the eyebrow row (always visible).

props.name: startExpanded
props.description:
Whether the hero (title + lede) starts expanded. Default true keeps every
existing caller unchanged; pass false to open collapsed — just the eyebrow
row (+ eyebrowActions) shows until the user expands it.

props.name: revealOnce
props.description:
Storage key enabling first-visit reveal: the hero opens the first time a
person lands on this page and stays collapsed on every visit after.
Omit to keep `startExpanded` as the only control. The explanation is
worth something once — this spends it then, not on visit two hundred.

props.name: collapsible
props.description:
Whether the hero can be opened at all. Pass false on a drill-down that
has nothing to reveal — the chevron disappears with the disclosure it
controlled, leaving the trail, the page name and the action strip. A
caret that opens nothing is a promise the page cannot keep.

props.name: contentMax
props.description:
The measure the header's content sits on, as a CSS length. Must match
whatever the page body below it uses, or the trail and the first card
start on different left edges.
Defaults to the 1600px column. Pass `'none'` for a full-bleed page (the
dashboards do this): above ~1600px of content area the capped column
centres itself, which spends ~50px a side on nothing before the body's
own gutter even starts.

props.name: gutter
props.description:
The header's own side gutter, as a CSS length. Must match the page body
below it or the trail and the first card start on different left edges.
Defaults to 1.5rem, which dates from the header living outside the
shell's PagePanel. It renders inside PagePanel now, so that default is
added to PagePanel's own 2rem — pass `'0'` (and drop the body's `px-6`)
to let PagePanel be the single gutter instead of the third one.

props.name: narrow
props.description: Constrain content to a readable narrow width (≤ 760px).

props.name: header
props.description: Full override for the header bar — takes precedence over title/actions.

props.name: title
props.description: Auto-generated mono header label. Ignored when header snippet is provided.

props.name: icon
props.description: Glyph rendered before `title`, naming the card's subject at a glance.

props.name: actions
props.description: Right-aligned content in the auto-generated header row.

props.name: footer
props.description: Rendered in a bordered footer bar below the body.

props.name: tone
props.description: Card tint. Defaults to the neutral elevated surface.

props.name: shape
props.description:
The header/outline composition. Defaults to the rounded rectangle with a
rule near the top. See `PanelShape`.

props.name: flush
props.description:
Drop the header's divider and raised background so it reads as a label
inside the card rather than a titlebar on top of it. Suits dense
config surfaces where a divider per card adds rules but no meaning.

props.name: allowOverflow
props.description:
Let absolutely-positioned children (hover popovers, dropdowns, tooltips)
escape the card bounds. Off by default so the header/footer stay clipped
to the rounded corners; the header/footer get matching corner rounding
when enabled so they still read as a card.

props.name: padding
props.description:
Body padding. `dense` is for surfaces that stack many panels in a narrow
rail — a HUD, an inspector column — where the default 16px gutter spends
more of the rail on air than on content. `none` hands the padding to the
child, for a panel wrapping a list or a canvas that must reach the edge.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes forwarded to the root element.

props.name: trailing
props.description:
Pushed to the far end of the strip — a control that belongs to the
 readings rather than a reading of its own.

props.name: chip
props.description: Console-chip styling: cut-corner clip-path, sharp aesthetic. Default is rounded marketing tile.

props.name: indeterminate
props.description: Neither on nor off — for a box standing in for a partly-selected set.

props.name: value
props.description: Current set of selected chip values.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Suggestions shown in the dropdown (filtered by query).

props.name: placeholder
props.default: 'Drag & drop, paste, or click to browse'

props.name: error
props.description: Inline error message — shows below the field with red styling.

props.name: showOptional
props.description: Render a muted "(optional)" tag after the label when not required.

props.name: id
props.description: Should match the id on the child input for label association.

props.name: status
props.description: Visual state — drives border + focus color.

props.name: min
props.description: Numeric constraints — forwarded to `<input>`; `type="number"` only.

props.name: options
props.description: The ordered set. Order is the step order — it is what ‹ and › walk.

props.name: value
props.description: The selected `value`. An unknown value lands on the first option.

props.name: onpick
props.description: Called with the newly selected `value`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group, e.g. "Impact".

props.name: wrap
props.description:
Step past the ends and come around. Off by default: for a scale
(low → critical) wrapping from the top back to the bottom is a
misclick waiting to happen, and the disabled chevron is what tells you
you are at the end. Turn it on for a set with no natural extremes.

props.name: width
props.description: Width of the whole control. A row of them aligns when this matches.

props.name: color
props.description: Colour for the value text — a per-value hue, if the set carries one.

props.name: class
props.description: Extra classes on the host, so a page can place it.

props.name: cut
props.description: Which corners are chamfered — the chip's meaning. See the header.

props.name: cutSize
props.description: Chamfer depth. Under 3px the cut reads as a rendering artefact.

props.name: edge
props.description:
How the outline is drawn: continuous hairline, HUD corner ticks, or
 nothing at all (fill-only, for chips packed into a dense table).

props.name: lead
props.description:
The leading marker. `dot` is the legacy signal; `bar` and `wedge` are
 painted inside the clip, so they take the silhouette's cut with them.

props.name: pulse
props.description:
Animates the `dot` lead. Kept as its own prop because call sites read
 `pulse` as "this is live", not as "put a dot here".

props.name: outline
props.description: Wraps the chip in an animated RGB conic-gradient outline.

props.name: cut
props.description:
Which silhouette the studio opens on — every way in from the page has
 its own, and landing on the wrong one is a hunt.

props.name: action
props.description: Optional action (e.g. a danger Button) placed at the right end.

props.name: sub
props.description: Optional sub-text shown below the message.

props.name: variant
